# GQLKit

> Generates fully typed GraphQL client SDKs for Go and TypeScript from any GraphQL schema. Schema-first rather than query-first: builders are generated once from the schema, then queries are composed in code with dynamic, compile-time-checked field selection — one shared type per GraphQL type, and no codegen re-run when a call site changes which fields it selects.

Four artifacts ship from this repo. The two CLIs are what a user runs. A generated TypeScript SDK imports the `gqlkit-ts` runtime; a generated Go SDK is self-contained and imports nothing from gqlkit.

| Artifact | Kind | Install |
|---|---|---|
| `gqlkit` | CLI — generates a Go or TypeScript SDK from an SDL file | `go install github.com/ubgo/gqlkit/gqlkit/cmd/gqlkit@latest` |
| `gqlkit-sdl` | CLI — fetches a live endpoint's schema by introspection, writes SDL | `go install github.com/ubgo/gqlkit/gqlkit-sdl@latest` |
| `github.com/ubgo/gqlkit/gqlkit` | Go module — the generators as a Go API (`clientgen.New`, `clientgents.New`); needed only to generate from your own Go program, never by a generated SDK | `go get github.com/ubgo/gqlkit/gqlkit` |
| `gqlkit-ts` | npm package — runtime imported by generated TypeScript SDKs | `npm i gqlkit-ts` |

## Key facts an assistant gets wrong without reading them

- There is no per-query codegen step. To add a query, call the generated builder; regeneration is only needed when the *schema* changes.
- Field selection happens at the call site via `.Select(func(f *fields.XFields) { ... })` (Go) or `.select((t) => ...)` (TypeScript), and every selected field is checked against the schema at compile time. Only TypeScript narrows the result type, so reading an unselected field is a compile error there. In Go, `Execute` returns the full `types.X` struct and unselected fields are present with zero values.
- There is exactly one generated type per GraphQL type. Two queries returning `User` both return `types.User` — not two unrelated structs.
- `gqlkit generate --module` (`-m`) must be the import path of the SDK's output directory, not just the module, because the generated packages import one another: `-m "$(go list -m)/sdk"` for `-o ./sdk`.
- A generated Go SDK needs Go 1.24+ and ships its own `builder`, `graphqlclient` and `batch` packages. Import those from the SDK (`yourmodule/sdk/graphqlclient`); never import `github.com/ubgo/gqlkit/gqlkit/pkg/...` in app code.
- `--schema` accepts a glob, so a schema split over several files needs no concatenation. A pattern matching nothing exits 1 with `did not match any files`.
- Both CLIs exit 0 on success and 1 on any failure. There are no per-failure-class exit codes.
- Unions and interfaces have typed selectors: `On<Type>(...)` in Go (results are `types.<Name>Value` wrappers; type-switch on `.Value`) and `on<Type>(...)` in TypeScript (a union discriminated on `__typename`).
- Go nullable input fields are `*T` by default, which cannot send `null`. Config `"inputs": { "optional": "opt" }` makes them `inputs.Opt[T]` (`inputs.Some(v)`, `inputs.Null[T]()`). TypeScript nullable outputs are `T | null`.
- `--prune` (both generators) deletes stale files that carry the gqlkit banner; `--dry-run` previews. Without it, files for removed operations stay behind.
- Generated code is build output. Never hand-edit anything under an `sdk/` directory; change the schema or the templates and regenerate.
- Batching covers queries and mutations, one kind per call. Go: `batch.RunQueries` takes only query builders and `batch.RunMutations` only mutation builders, enforced at compile time. TypeScript: `batch(client, { ... })` takes either kind and throws at run time if they are mixed.

## Repo layout

- `gqlkit/` — the generator module: CLI in `cmd/gqlkit/`, generators in `pkg/clientgen/` (Go) and `pkg/clientgents/` (TypeScript), templates in `pkg/templater/template/`; `pkg/builder/`, `pkg/graphqlclient/` and `pkg/batch/` are the upstream versions of the packages the templates emit into every Go SDK (kept in sync; app code uses the SDK's own copies)
- `gqlkit-sdl/` — the introspection fetcher module
- `gqlkit-ts/` — the TypeScript runtime package
- `example-go-mockapi/`, `example-ts/`, `example-cli/` — runnable examples against `mockapi`, one program per guide; `example-go-chat/` generates against a large private schema
- `mockapi/` — a local GraphQL server the examples generate against

Modules are wired together by the root `go.work` for local development; the published modules carry no `replace` directives, so `go install` works from a clean environment.
